Where and why the h5/h10 forecasts go bad (TEST split)

Test window 2024-10-18 → 2026-08-14. Realized = actual Parkinson variance on day t (identical across horizons). y_pred at horizon h is the forecast FOR day t made h days earlier, so a larger h uses staler information.

A. Where the QLIKE damage is — per realized-vol decile (SP500 + VN)

At the daily horizon h1 the deep model beats HAR-X on every decile (curve below 0). At h5/h10 it still beats HAR-X on the calm deciles D0-D4 but flips to worse (red zone, >0) on the storm deciles D5-D9. On S&P 500 the storm-decile penalty reaches +0.13 (h5) / +0.15 (h10) at D9. Those storm-decile losses are exactly the cells that erase the deep model's h5/h10 edge.

B. Why — the deep forecast is a spike echo delayed by ~h days

S&P 500 — storm episode (MCHP, peak 2025-04-09)

Black = realized. The LSTM forecast at h1 (blue) reacts to the spike ~1 day late; at h5 (orange) it reacts ~5 days late; at h10 (red) ~10 days late. Because the reaction is shifted by the horizon, at h5/h10 the forecast peaks on days when the market has already reverted to calm (shaded) — i.e. it over-forecasts the post-storm tail, the D5-D9 cells of Section A. HAR-X h10 (grey dashed) is a flatter long-memory average that reverts sooner, so it eats a smaller QLIKE penalty on those tail days. No model anticipates day-0 (VN storms are exogenous), so the h5/h10 damage is the mis-timed echo, not the missed spike itself.
